about: Proposed region definitions for detailed maps of Czechia: 14 regions (kraje), one region each. See docs/REGIONS-CZ.md.

codes.proposal: Current ISO 3166-2:CZ codes: CZ-10 (Prague), CZ-20, CZ-31, CZ-32, CZ-41, CZ-42, CZ-51, CZ-52, CZ-53, CZ-63, CZ-64, CZ-71, CZ-72, CZ-80.
codes.why: These are the codes ISO 3166-2:CZ defines today (two digits per region). The letter codes CZ-PR, CZ-JC, CZ-JM, CZ-KA, CZ-KR, CZ-LI, CZ-OL, CZ-PA, CZ-PL, CZ-ST, CZ-US, CZ-VY, CZ-ZL and CZ-MO were replaced by the numeric ones in November 2016 and are no longer ISO codes. A bare CZ is not in STATE_CODES (engine/address_search.py); PR, MO and PA are (Puerto Rico, Missouri, Pennsylvania), and US is the ISO 3166-1 code of the United States.
codes.verified: opened 2026-11-18: OMG's ISO 3166-2 ontology for Czechia, which reproduces the ISO list and defines exactly these 14 units with no letter code. The 2016-11-15 date of the replacement is unverified: the ISO Online Browsing Platform answers HTTP 403, so the change log could only be read in Wikipedia's copy of it. Not checked against the ISO site.
codes.open_question: The numeric code part fails the [A-Z]{2} rule for address indexes (engine/setup/manifest.py line 72, engine/setup/install.py line 267) and the [A-Z]{2} dispatch in packaging/build_packs.py build_map().

CC-BY-4.0.name: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International
CC-BY-4.0.attribution: ČÚZK asks for the source in the form "ČÚZK, [rok]" (year of the data used) in printed outputs from the data and in viewing services over them; the metadata passed on and a description of any change to a modified work are duties tied to dissemination ("šířit"). A private copy triggers none of them.
CC-BY-4.0.attribution_sentence: data printouts and viewing services including these data must contain the source in the form „ČÚZK “ where time information is related to the updatedness of the particular dataset.
CC-BY-4.0.attribution_sentence_note: Opened 2026-11-18 on the English version of ČÚZK's terms page, "Version 1.0 - dated April 4, 2016". That page is stale: it names no CC BY 4.0, lists no ZABAGED and drops the [rok] placeholder, so the Czech page is the one to quote. No worked example on either page; not checked on the CC site.

terrain.dataset: DMR 5G (digital relief model, 5th generation), LAZ per SM5 map sheet
terrain.notes: Airborne laser scanning 2009-2013, completed 2016-06-30; mean height error 0.18 m in open terrain, 0.3 m under forest; S-JTSK / Bpv; no fixed update cycle, product last updated 2026-06-01. A point cloud: needs rasterisation before tools/build_terrain.py can read it.

terrain.dataset: DMR 4G (digital relief model, 4th generation), regular 5 x 5 m grid, TIFF and LAZ per SM5 map sheet
terrain.verified: opened 2026-11-18 (product page and TIFF Atom service)
terrain.notes: Mean height error 0.3 m in open terrain, 1 m under forest; Bpv heights; TIFF Atom service DMR4G-SJTSK-TIFF. 5 m is finer than the US 1 arc-second (~30 m). One file per SM5 sheet; one sheet measured at 768,908 bytes (BENE09).

terrain.notes: INSPIRE_EL_GRID_3045.zip, 7,685,616,237 bytes: the service feed says the data are TIFF and that the dataset is compressed for download (ZIP), and states no uncompressed size. Grid spacing not stated on the feed; neither was checked.

terrain.verified: opened 2026-11-18 (collection page); licence text not checked
terrain.notes: Surface model: relief follows canopy and roofs. Czechia tile completeness not checked.

crops.dataset: LPIS public export: farmer blocks (DPB), physical blocks (PB), vineyards (OPV), landscape features (EVP), SHP
crops.notes: Weekly generation, SHP per cadastral territory or per district, plus XML (current and historic). Declared land use, so areas are exact sums, not satellite pixels. Vineyards are a separate entity (OPV).
crops.status: Not copyrighted (work), not copyrighted (database), not protected (sui generis rights) — the data.gov.cz record cited, which is the Prague district dataset, not a national one. MZe's export page states no licence either, only the legal basis, Act 252/1997 Sb. § 3a; the record's DPB/XML distributions are marked "Contains personal data".

crops.verified: opened 2026-11-18 (repository page); licence text not reopened
crops.notes: Czechia is one of the participating countries. Share-alike: a crop layer built from it inherits CC BY-SA 4.0.

buildings.dataset: ZABAGED (fundamental base of geographic data), GeoPackage, whole state, one ZIP
buildings.notes: Zip: 5,805,826,649 bytes in S-JTSK (EPSG:5514), 6,742,892,709 bytes in ETRS89/TM33 (EPSG:3045), dated 2026-10-04. The GeoPackage is one of the selected formats ČÚZK serves through its ATOM service, i.e. open data since 2023-07-01; other formats and media stay in the e-shop. Building outlines are one of the 142 planimetric feature types; the layer name was not confirmed.

buildings.notes: Built daily where an obec changed. One file per obec, roughly 6,258 of them, so a whole country means a merge step. No heights.

buildings.verified: opened 2026-11-18 for the attribution page; the Czech mix of sources is not described there and was not checked

buildings.dataset: Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints, regions CzechRepublic and Czechia
buildings.notes: The 2026-11-12 dataset-links.csv lists 225 regions and files Czechia under two names, CzechRepublic (47 rows) and Czechia (41 rows), over 49 distinct quadkeys; a fill filter has to match both. No heights for Czechia were confirmed.

postal_code.format: Five digits, written as three digits, one space, two digits: "110 00", "602 00".
postal_code.source: Česká pošta, "Provedení a úprava adresní strany obálek a psaní", opened 2026-11-18: "Mezi trojčíslím a dvojčíslím PSČ je jedna mezera"

addressing.order: Street, then house number, then postcode and town on the last line ("Karlova 12, 110 00 Praha 1"); the postcode and the delivery place share the last line, and the name of the část obce may be added to the obec.
addressing.house_numbers: Two numbers in one address: číslo popisné (descriptive number, unique within a část obce) and číslo orientační (orientation number within a street), written "1234/56" and often with a letter ("12a", "56/3b"). RÚIAN keeps them as separate fields (CisloDomovni, CisloOrientacni, CisloOrientacniPismeno) plus a type (č.p. or č.ev.).
addressing.notes: normalize() in engine/address_search.py keeps only a-z and 0-9, so "náměstí" becomes "n m st" and "Česká" becomes "esk"; is_address_query() needs a digit first, and Czech addresses start with the street; _parts() reads a postcode only as the last word and only as five digits without a space, while the PSČ comes before the town and carries a space; tools/build_addresses.py keeps only country = 'US' and cuts the postcode to five characters. Read in this repository on 2026-11-18.
